topics.name: SQL Queries
scenarios: A university registration system stores students, modules, lecturers, and semester enrollments, including students repeating modules.
A hospital appointment system records patients, doctors, departments, visits, and cancellations across multiple branches.
An online marketplace tracks customers, sellers, orders, products, returns, and discounts over several financial quarters.
A transport operator maintains routes, vehicles, drivers, trips, and passenger bookings, including cancelled services.

topics.name: Database Indexing
scenarios: A banking system processes millions of transactions while users frequently search accounts by date range and branch.
A healthcare platform retrieves patient records using patient identifiers, appointment dates, and department filters.
An e-commerce catalogue receives frequent product updates while shoppers filter by category, price, and availability.
A university learning platform queries large submission tables by module, student, submission time, and grading status.

topics.name: Case Study Requirements
scenarios: A municipal council plans an online permit application system involving residents, inspectors, and finance officers.
A private hospital replaces paper-based laboratory requests with a system shared by clinicians and technicians.
A logistics company wants to coordinate delivery assignments, customer notifications, and proof of delivery.
A university plans a research supervision portal supporting students, supervisors, and examination panels.

topics.name: UML and Design Decisions
scenarios: A hotel booking platform must coordinate room inventory, payments, cancellations, and administrator overrides.
A vehicle rental service manages reservations, inspections, late returns, and maintenance schedules.
A pharmacy inventory platform tracks suppliers, stock batches, expiry dates, and prescription fulfillment.
A sports tournament system schedules matches, registers teams, records scores, and publishes standings.

topics.name: Project Selection
scenarios: A university must prioritize three digital services under a fixed annual technology budget.
A retail company evaluates competing inventory automation proposals with different costs and delivery timelines.
A hospital compares patient scheduling projects using operational benefits, implementation risks, and resource constraints.
A public transport authority evaluates alternative ticketing upgrades with conflicting stakeholder priorities.

topics.name: Project Risk and Control
scenarios: A mobile banking project faces changing regulations, a delayed vendor integration, and limited testing capacity.
A campus management system has missed two milestones because requirements were approved late.
A distributed development team encounters staff turnover, unstable dependencies, and repeated scope changes.
A healthcare software project reports rising defect counts while its deployment deadline remains fixed.

topics.name: User Research and Design Thinking
scenarios: A public hospital redesigns its appointment website for older adults and first-time smartphone users.
A university investigates why students abandon its online module registration process.
A banking application team studies accessibility barriers faced by customers with visual impairments.
A grocery delivery startup investigates checkout failures among users with unreliable mobile connectivity.

topics.name: Hierarchical Task Analysis
scenarios: A railway ticket kiosk requires passengers to select routes, seats, payment methods, and ticket collection options.
A university portal allows students to submit assignments, verify uploads, and review submission receipts.
A clinic receptionist uses a patient registration workflow involving identity checks and appointment allocation.
A delivery driver application supports accepting jobs, navigation, proof of delivery, and exception reporting.

topics.name: REST API and Middleware
scenarios: A campus event application exposes endpoints for event registration, capacity checks, and ticket cancellation.
A healthcare booking API requires role-based access, request validation, and consistent error responses.
A food delivery service needs middleware for authentication, request logging, and rate limiting.
An inventory management API supports pagination, filtering, and controlled updates to product quantities.

topics.name: Framework Debugging
scenarios: A web application returns unauthorized responses after a token refresh despite a valid user session.
A React interface displays stale order information after an asynchronous update request completes.
An Express application produces duplicate responses because error-handling middleware is ordered incorrectly.
A database-backed API intermittently fails when concurrent requests modify the same inventory item.

topics.name: Distributed Communication
scenarios: A ride-hailing platform coordinates location updates between drivers, passengers, and dispatch services.
A university examination platform distributes notifications across independently deployed services.
A warehouse network exchanges stock updates between regional systems with intermittent connectivity.
A payment platform processes requests across several services while preserving transaction identifiers.

topics.name: Dependability and Fault Tolerance
scenarios: A replicated hospital records service must remain available when one regional server becomes unreachable.
A ticket booking system experiences partial network failure while processing simultaneous seat reservations.
A distributed file storage service must recover from node crashes without losing acknowledged uploads.
An online payment workflow must handle retries after timeouts without charging customers twice.

topics.name: Architectural Styles and Trade-offs
scenarios: A small startup considers moving a monolithic ordering application to independently deployed services.
A national healthcare platform must balance availability, interoperability, security, and maintenance cost.
A university learning platform expects seasonal traffic spikes during examination submission periods.
A logistics company compares event-driven and request-response approaches for shipment tracking.

topics.name: Architecture Modeling
scenarios: A digital library requires a component view showing search, lending, authentication, and notification services.
A payment application needs a deployment model separating client devices, application servers, and databases.
A hospital information system requires interfaces between patient records, laboratories, and billing.
A travel booking platform needs a sequence model for reservations involving inventory and payment services.

topics.name: Specification-Based Testing
scenarios: A scholarship application accepts candidates based on age, academic results, and income thresholds.
A booking system applies different cancellation fees depending on the time remaining before departure.
A loan application validates salary ranges, employment categories, and repayment periods.
A university grading system converts numeric marks into grade bands using defined boundaries.

topics.name: Code-Based Testing
scenarios: An order discount function contains nested conditions for customer status and purchase value.
A password validation routine uses multiple Boolean conditions and early return statements.
A shipping cost function contains loops and branches based on weight, distance, and delivery priority.
A login throttling function tracks failed attempts and applies conditional account lockouts.
